a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: Ondansetron, the closest structural analog in the supplied records, has an absolute oral bioavailability of 50-65% after an 8 mg oral dose in fasted volunteers.
Additional human ondansetron records report oral bioavailability of approximately 59%, 50-70%, 60%, and 62 ± 15%, all consistently well above the 20% threshold.
No supplied record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20% for the query or its close ondansetron-class analogs; all relevant measured oral bioavailability values are 50-70%.

evidence_gaps: No direct alosetron-specific bioavailability record is present; the prediction relies on transfer from closely related ondansetron records.
No fed/fasted or formulation-specific alosetron data are supplied, though ondansetron fasted and general oral data are consistent.
Alosetron-specific first-pass metabolism and solubility are not directly measured in the supplied records.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F >= 20%) because the query is a close ondansetron-class 5-HT3 antagonist with favorable physicochemical properties, and multiple ondansetron records show absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 50-70%, far above the threshold, with no affirmative low evidence.
